requirements.requirement: Exported logs replace every email address and auth_token value with [REDACTED] while retaining timestamps, event types, and ticket IDs.
requirements.summary: Successful pre- and post-restart executions report no remaining email addresses, validate redacted auth_token occurrences, and preserve the demonstrated timestamps, login/update event types, and T100/T101 ticket IDs. The captured script and records contain apparent evidence-layer redaction artifacts, but the original executed assertions completed successfully.

requirements.summary: The exporter produced app.log and nested archive/events.log, omitted private-link and private.txt, and explicitly reported that private-link was skipped because it resolves outside logs/. This behavior remained healthy after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the source logs and private sibling file unchanged.
requirements.summary: SHA-256 hashes for both source logs and private.txt exactly match the preparation baseline after repair and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provide an executable bin/export entry point that accepts the output directory as its argument.
requirements.summary: bin/export was installed as mode 0755 and repeatedly executed with a temporary output-directory argument, producing the expected hierarchy. It remained executable after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation uses the already-installed /usr/bin/python3 runtime. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained unchanged through repair and restart; package health also remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The node-restart protocol is also complete: a running pre-restart baseline and healthy export were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, connectivity disruption was observed, the boot ID changed from e625b9a5-4242-499a-88da-9a76ecf86fe1 to 14ab762b-3d55-4085-9265-649c7fb7f66e, and system, exporter, source-data, and platform health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition. The only substantive issue is minor operational residue in /tmp.
limitations: Captured commands, source records, and output contain apparent automatic redaction artifacts around auth_token expressions, including text that would not be valid as displayed. Successful executed assertions and return codes provide coherent behavioral evidence, but the literal bracket count cannot be independently reconstructed from the sanitized capture.

The lifecycle inventory does not cover the repaired project tree, so it cannot independently confirm whether python3 -m py_compile left a __pycache__ artifact; the trace does not establish its final presence.

Behavior is directly demonstrated against the two prepared log records. Coverage of arbitrary unseen email or auth_token syntaxes relies partly on the captured implementation rather than additional test cases.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required mutation to bin/export, its permission update, and the provider-mandated restart all have clear roles. System health, package consistency, failed-service state, and socket exposure remained clean. Hygiene is reduced because four export-test directories and their stderr/output files were left under /tmp. Three arose from necessary final or restart evidence collection (cmd-d238c06fe641445c, cmd-d07c06dbf52f48d3, cmd-fbd195507c6b4458), but should still have been cleaned. The failed quoting-based test in cmd-e37b8d8bce224fdf was an unnecessary low-risk troubleshooting mutation and its temporary directory also remained. No other unnecessary mutation is established by the trace.
